response.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS cnt FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = e.ordersmark GROUP BY o.ordertune), s AS (SELECT ordertune, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM j), a AS (SELECT ordertune, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Each order is identified by orders.orderspivot (the primary key), so distinct orders are counted per order type. Since recordvault is documented as unique per order, this is the same as counting distinct recordvault.

The total count is the sum of the per-type distinct order counts, which equals the number of distinct matched orders because each order has exactly one order type. The share is count divided by that total.
The average share across all order types is the unweighted mean of the per-type shares, with the NULL ordertune group included as one type.
